result.title: Refining Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation via Regional Semantics and Visual Prototypes
result.summary: Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) has shown superior performance in the image-level open-vocabulary classification task, benefiting from its powerful alignment of visual features and text embeddings. However, dense prediction tasks require models to perform pixel-level predictions, necessitating modifications to CLIP for region-text alignment. In this paper, we adjust the attention layers within the vanilla visual encoder of CLIP. With a novel attention calculation method for selective attention features, the model retains more regional semantic information. To further mitigate the negative impact of the modality gap, we introduce additional visual prototypes to refine the original predictor solely based on text embeddings. Specifically, patch features with confident predictions are selected to form an additional auxiliary memory-based classifier for more accurate prediction. We further integrate an optimizable feature extractor with an exponential moving average updating strategy to enhance prediction quality. Extensive experiments on $5$ semantic segmentation datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

AI.brief_summary: 针对 CLIP 在开放词表语义分割中区域-文本对齐不足的问题，改造视觉编码器注意力以保留区域语义，并引入由高置信 patch 特征构成的视觉原型辅助分类器，配合 EMA 更新的可优化特征提取器提升像素级预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 用置信度筛选 patch 特征构建辅助记忆分类器、并以 EMA 维护特征提取器，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与辅助读出状态的设计提供可核查线索，但原文并无推理期 latent 状态或动态计算。
